title: Employment Situation (Sep 2027 data) — 08:30 ET, the first payroll after the September SEP meeting and a late-in-the-month release the rule pushes to the second Friday
source: EST: derived from BLS's own published scheduling rule — release on the third Friday following the end of the reference week (the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th) — using the implementation jobs-2027-09-03's own initial research re-wrote and re-validated from scratch on 2026-09-09, 7 for 7 against the four confirmed jobs-* entries on this calendar (2026-09-04, 2026-10-02, 2026-11-06, 2026-12-04) and the three historical Sunday-July-4 releases (2004-07-02, 2010-07-02, 2021-07-02). September 2027's 12th is a SUNDAY, so the reference week is Sun 2027-09-12 to Sat 2027-09-18 and the third Friday after 09-18 is 2027-10-08 — a second-Friday release rather than the usual first-Friday one. The rule emits the identical shape whenever a September 12th falls on a Sunday (1993, 2004, 2010 and 2021 all resolve to an October 8 release), so this is the rule behaving normally, not an edge case. The prefix is EST: and not BLS: because bls.gov returned HTTP 403 on all four schedule routes re-tried on 2026-09-09 and fred.stlouisfed.org failed to connect — recorded in jobs-2027-09-03's probe-ref.blocked. A derived date is not a published one
notes: PROPOSED BY jobs-2027-09-03's initial research (2026-09-09) at D+35 — well outside the 5-day corridor, and proposed anyway because it is the fact that makes the proposer's own structural leg checkable: with no payroll between 2027-09-03 and the 2027-09-15 FOMC, jobs-2027-09-03 is the LAST payroll the September SEP meeting sees, and jobs-2027-08-06 the first. Without this date on the calendar that claim is unfalsifiable. TWO THINGS A LATER LANE SHOULD NOT HAVE TO REDISCOVER. (1) THE DATE LOOKS WRONG AND IS NOT. Every other payroll on this calendar lands on a first Friday; this one lands on the second because the 12th of the reference month is a Sunday, which pushes the Sun-Sat reference week a full seven days later than a same-month Saturday-12th would. The same rule, unchanged, emits an October 8 release for every Sunday-September-12th year it is run over (1993, 2004, 2010, 2021). Do not 'correct' it to 2027-10-01. None of those four is a primary-verified known — the 7-for-7 validation set is the four confirmed jobs-* calendar entries plus the three Sunday-July-4 releases — so this is the rule reproducing its own documented behaviour, which is weaker evidence than a fetched schedule and is labelled as such. (2) ITS SEASONAL PROFILE IS UNTESTED HERE. jobs-2027-08-06 measured August (amplification rank 1 of 12 in TLT/IEF/AGG) and jobs-2027-09-03 measured September (ranks 11/12 SPY, 12/12 QQQ, 11/12 IEF) and found them opposite; October was not measured by either and must not be assumed to resemble the month on either side of it. HONEST LIMITS. Filed status estimate and it must stay there until bls.gov's 2027 schedule is retrievable; this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep, and the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a derived date. impact high and symbols [] match every other jobs-* entry. Estimates widen caution and license no entry.
